title: Metabolomic and proteomic responses of different biological tissues to intense physical exercise
summary:
During physical exertion, the body responds with various adaptations. In addition to changes in breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure, certain substances in the body also change, which can provide clues about exertion and recovery. Such substances can help better assess training loads and plan recovery times more effectively. This information is particularly important in competitive sports. Until now, this has often required blood samples or muscle tissue analyses. However, these procedures are time-consuming and, in some cases, invasive.
The aim of this study is to investigate how certain substances in the body change after intense physical exertion and whether saliva or urine samples provide similar information to blood or muscle samples. The goal is to determine whether saliva and urine can be used in the future as simple and less invasive alternatives.
For the study, participants will complete an intense training session on a treadmill. Blood, saliva, urine, and muscle samples will be collected at multiple time points before and within 24 hours after the exercise and compared with one another. In addition, exercise data such as heart rate will be recorded. Subsequently, the study will examine how the measured substances change in the various samples and how closely the results correlate with one another.

interventions.name: Intervention group: Sprint interval training on a treadmill on study day 3 with continuous monitoring of respiratory gases and heart rate. Passive control group: No physical intervention. Participants remain seated and at rest for the duration of the study period, corresponding to the length of the training intervention for the intervention group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Signing the consent form
Exclusion criteria:
Acute infections or orthopedic issues that make spiroergometric exercise testing impossible; the presence of a pacemaker or an ongoing pregnancy, as these conditions make it impossible to perform a bioimpedance analysis to assess body composition;  insufficient knowledge of German, as this makes it impossible to complete the questionnaire;
chronic pre-existing conditions, regular medication use, a blood donation within the past 56 days (see https://www.blutspendedienst-west.de/presse/faq-zum-blutspendedienst), or the use of allergy medications (antihistamines).
